description: A dog that would not stop waiting. Its crooked jaw hangs loose, grinning at a joke told before it came.
lore: The joke was not funny. A long one about a neighbour and a borrowed ladder, with the same wrong pause in the middle every time, told to the same dog most evenings for nine years by a hill farmer with no one else to try it on. The dog did not have the joke. The dog had the last two seconds of it: the man's own laugh going off like a dropped pan, a hand coming down heavy on its head, then supper. That is a complete world, if you are a dog.

Then the farmer's turn came, and the dog's came after, and the dog [[lore/the_waking|woke in the meadow grass]] like everything else that arrives here. It waited. He was not there, and he was not there the next season, and past a certain point the word for a man like that is the heaviest one in the language: he is one of the unwoken.
A dog cannot draw a conclusion from that. It is the only mercy in the business.

So it waits at the head of any track that climbs toward a farm — hide gone patchy, ribs standing out, something green lifting off its spine in the cold — and through all of it the jaw has not slipped a hair, hung open and crooked and full of teeth, fixed in the two seconds before a hand comes down. People have tried feeding it. It is not hungry. It wants the two seconds.
gm_notes: Description rewritten: the shipped line said 'too stubborn to stay buried' and 'before it died', and nothing here is buried and nothing dies — it came, the way everything comes. The grin is the record: a learned reflex outliving the man who trained it. He is unwoken, which is stated flatly and never explained, and the dog is incapable of the arithmetic a person would do in its place — keep it that way. Root-free leaf otherwise; the farmer needs no name and should never get one. No stone or leavings bound yet.
